newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PM SAYS SUPPORTS NEW 1998 BUDGET CUTS - STT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PM SAYS SUPPORTS NEW 1998 BUDGET CUTS - STT.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen at the weekend voiced support for new spending cuts proposed by the finance ministry prior to the August 13 start of the government's 1998 state budget negotiations, the Finnish news agency STT reported.
It quoted a speech and a newspaper interview with Lipponen.
"The finance ministry is on the right track," Lipponen said.

"Now the tightening is around a couple billion markka. That is modest compared with the need, but it is a good achievement in itself," he said. The finance ministry has proposed cutting budget spending by 3-4 billion markka to 188 billion markka.

Lipponen supported the finance ministry's view that new expenditure cuts were necessary to reduce the state's net borrowing. If the planned cuts were implemented, net borrowing would be around 17 billion markka in 1998, down from an estimated 26 billion this year.
